hero.title: Public Health in Mauritius
hero.subtitle: **Public Health in Mauritius for Indian Students** is a study pathway for students interested in disease prevention, health promotion, epidemiology, healthcare policy and improving health at the community and population levels. Unlike clinical degrees focused primarily on treating individual patients, public health programmes examine how health systems, environments, behaviours and social conditions affect entire communities. Students who want to **Study Public Health in Mauritius** can explore postgraduate opportunities and related academic pathways.

overview: The Master of Public Health (MPH) is a relevant postgraduate option for graduates in medicine, nursing, pharmacy, biology, environmental sciences and other eligible disciplines. The University of Mauritius has published an MPH programme, while the Open University of Mauritius has documented an MPH offered in collaboration with Imperial College London. Applicants must verify the current intake, programme arrangements and fees before applying. **Edu-Hawk Worldwide** encourages students to check the latest admission and programme details before making a decision.

faq.question: Can Indian students study an MPH in Mauritius?
faq.answer: Indian students can apply if they meet the institution’s academic and international admission requirements. They should confirm the next intake, international tuition fees and student-entry arrangements directly with the university. Edu-Hawk Worldwide can help students understand the admission considerations for Public Health in Mauritius for Indian Students.

faq.question: How long does an MPH take in Mauritius?
faq.answer: The Open University of Mauritius lists a duration of 21 to 39 months for its published MPH programme. The actual duration depends on the programme structure and the student’s study plan.

faq.question: What is the cost of studying public health in Mauritius?
faq.answer: The fee depends on the institution and student category. The published MUR 300,000 fee at the Open University of Mauritius is for Mauritian students; an international non-SADC fee is not specified on that page. Request a current international quotation.

faq.question: Can I study public health after MBBS, nursing or pharmacy?
faq.answer: Yes, these backgrounds may be relevant for MPH admission, subject to the university’s entry requirements. The published Open University programme lists medicine, nursing, pharmacy and other health-related backgrounds among its accepted subject areas.

faq.question: What jobs can I get after an MPH in Mauritius?
faq.answer: Possible pathways include public health research, epidemiology, health programme management, health promotion, policy analysis and monitoring and evaluation. Specific roles may require relevant work experience, additional qualifications or professional registration.
